_tuning_notes: River hippo, the territory tank. territory.radius = aggro zone in blocks around the water-anchored claim (anchor 'water' snaps the center to the nearest water within 8 at spawn; 'spawn' uses the spawn spot); aggro_inside=false would make it decorative. Intruders (survival players, boats) get a 3s yawn warning, then a charge; calms ~20s after the zone empties. knockback feeds ATTACK_KNOCKBACK. Boats die in 2 bites and drop planks+sticks (hardcoded drama). Babies are leashed to half the radius. Phase 3: breed_item melon (also the cage bait); cage_tier 2. RARITY: tier 'uncommon' supplies the spawn weight; group_size and nearby_cap are pinned here (2-4, cap 6). nearby_cap denies natural spawns when that many of this animal are already within 64 blocks — the fix for persistent CREATURE mobs accumulating forever. ECOLOGY 0.4.2: rivers only, minus frozen rivers (a hippo does not live under ice). aquatic=true records that this species uses the water-line spawn placement; tools/spawn-lint.py fails the build if that flag and the Java placement disagree. BABY SIZE 0.4.2: baby_scale moved 0.5 -> 1.0. The client already bakes the baby mesh through vanilla's BabyModelTransform (body halved, head full size) and vanilla age scaling halves the hitbox, so a 0.5 here was a SECOND shrink and calves rendered at a quarter of adult size. 1.0 = vanilla baby proportions. SIZE PASS 0.4.6: scale set against MEASURED vanilla hitboxes rather than by eye (cow 0.90x1.40, horse 1.40x1.60, polar bear 1.40x1.40, ravager 1.95x2.20, wolf 0.60x0.85, turtle 1.20x0.40, ocelot 0.60x0.70, chicken 0.40x0.70). Attributes.SCALE is uniform and multiplies the MODEL and the HITBOX together, so this is the one lever that cannot desync them. ravager 1.95x2.20 -> 1.13x width, 0.85x height: ravager-class bulk, lower and broader. 2.4x cow width, 1.57x horse width. SIZE PASS revised: the first attempt scaled an already-wrong box. Measuring the baked meshes showed the hitboxes never matched the models — the hippo mesh was 1.06 blocks tall inside a 1.60 box (66% fill, a third of it empty air), while the gorilla mesh was LARGER than its hitbox (121%). Builder dimensions in MenagerieEntities now match the measured mesh, and this scale multiplies model and hitbox together from there, so the drawn animal fills the box it is struck in.
guide_blurb: Kills more boats than any reef.
